q: How do I calculate the emissions of a hospital PSA oxygen plant?
title: Hospital PSA oxygen plant emissions
short: A PSA oxygen plant runs on electricity, mainly its air compressor. Multiply the plant's kWh from a sub-meter by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, add generator diesel during outages, and divide by cubic metres of oxygen produced. Bought liquid oxygen is Scope 3 instead.

ul: The air compressor, the largest load.
The oxygen booster where cylinders are filled.

p: Oxygen made on site counts through the plant's electricity, in Scope 2. Liquid or cylinder oxygen bought from a supplier is a purchased good in Scope 3, Category 1.
Report kg CO2 per cubic metre from the plant's flow meter, and keep the sub-meter readings as evidence.

example.title: Worked example: hospital PSA plant (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Total: 10,650 / 9,000 = 1.183 kg CO2 per cubic metre
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use the plant sub-meter and flow meter readings.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
